---
title: "Under a normal model, what proportion exceeds a cutoff?"
---

## Question

Under a normal model, what proportion exceeds a cutoff?

## Work through it

Confirm mean and positive sd; mark the cutoff; compute the right-tail probability instead of the left-tail area.

## Worked example: airquality

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
mu <- mean(d$Temp)
sigma <- sd(d$Temp)
result <- ru_apply("normal_right_tail", mu=mu, sigma=sigma,
                   threshold=90, assume_normal=TRUE)
stopifnot(result>=0,result<=1)
```

This returns the modeled area above 90°F. It should be compared with the recorded fraction of days above 90°F before deciding whether the normal approximation fits.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("normal_right_tail", mu=your_mean, sigma=your_sd, threshold=your_cutoff, assume_normal=TRUE)
```

For a continuous normal model P(X>90) and P(X>=90) coincide. The distinction matters for discrete distributions.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("normal_right_tail")` before treating a calculation as an inference.

[Run the standalone script](../examples/normal_right_tail.R)
